item.title: ‘I Actually Thought He Was Going to Hit Me,’ OpenAI’s Greg Brockman Says of Elon Musk
item.description: OpenAI’s president wrapped his testimony on Tuesday by revealing a fiery meeting with Musk in 2017 and subsequent efforts to remove several board members.

item.title: Google DeepMind Workers Vote to Unionize Over Military AI Deals
item.description: UK staff of Google’s AI research lab hope to block the use of the company’s artificial intelligence models in military settings.

item.title: He Couldn’t Land a Job Interview. Was AI to Blame?
item.description: Armed with some Python and a white-hot sense of injustice, one medical student spent six months trying to figure out whether an algorithm trashed his job application.

item.title: Greg Brockman Defends $30B OpenAI Stake: ‘Blood, Sweat, and Tears’
item.description: OpenAI’s cofounder and president revealed in federal court on Monday that he’s one of the largest individual stakeholders in the AI lab.

item.title: Disneyland Now Uses Face Recognition on Visitors
item.description: Plus: The NSA tests Anthropic’s Mythos Preview to find vulnerabilities, a Finnish teen is charged over the Scattered Spider hacking spree, and more.

item.title: A Dark-Money Campaign Is Paying Influencers to Frame Chinese AI as a Threat
item.description: Build American AI, a nonprofit linked to a super PAC bankrolled by executives at OpenAI and Andreessen Horowitz, is funding a campaign to spread pro-AI messaging and stoke fears about China.

item.title: How Shivon Zilis Operated as Elon Musk’s OpenAI Insider
item.description: Messages presented at trial reveal how Zilis, the mother of four of Musk’s children, acted as an intermediary between him and OpenAI.

item.title: Good Luck Getting a Mac Mini for the Next ‘Several Months’
item.description: Apple CEO Tim Cook told analysts that AI adoption has happened faster than expected.

item.title: Musk v. Altman Kicks Off, DOJ Guts Voting Rights Unit, and Is the AI Job Apocalypse Overhyped?
item.description: In this episode of Uncanny Valley, we get into how the Elon Musk-Sam Altman trial goes way beyond their rivalry and could have major implications both for OpenAI and also the AI industry at large.

item.title: Elon Musk Seemingly Admits xAI Has Used OpenAI’s Models to Train Its Own
item.description: While answering questions under oath, Musk argued it’s standard practice for AI labs to use their competitors’ models.
